A schematic illustration of the production process is given in Fig. 1. The powder was gas atomized Ni-625 superalloy. It was obtained from Sandvik Osprey Metals Ltd. with a reported chemistry of 64.0Ni-20.9Cr-2.6Fe-3.2Nb-8.4Mo-0.01Al-0.01Co-0.029C-0.31Si-0.39Mn.
Initially, the Ni-625 powder and parafﬁn wax were mixed for 45 min. using a double-cone mixer heated to 373 K to melt the wax.
The mixtures were compacted at 150 MPa into cylinders with a diameter of 19 mm and height of 20 mm.

The parafﬁn wax was thermally removed as a part of the sintering cycle, which consisted of heating step-by-step at 1 K/min to 873 K with a 6 h hold, followed by heating at 5 K/min to 973 K for 1 h to pre-sinter the compacts. This was performed in high purity argon.
followed by heating at 5 K/min to 973 K for 1 h to pre-sinter the compacts. This was performed in high purity argon.
Subsequent ﬁnal sintering relied on a heating rate of 10 K/min to 1573 K for 1 h under vacuum (10/C02 Pa).

The foams were observed to contain mainly two types of pores: macropores obtained as a result of carbamide space-holder, and micropores on cell-walls, presumably resulting from the compaction and sintering process during the production of the Ni-625 superalloy foam.

there are two types of pores in Ni-625 foams: the interconnected spheroidal macropores with the size in the range of 800-1000 lm and the micropores with an average size in the range of 10-50 lm.

there are two types of pores in Ni-625 foams: the interconnected spheroidal macropores with the size in the range of 800-1000 lm and the micropores with an average size in the range of 10-50 lm. The micropores are irregularly distributed on the wall of the open interpenetrated macropores.
